newsitem.title: USA: Kennedy babysitter family urges end to probe.
newsitem.headline: Kennedy babysitter family urges end to probe.

text.p: The family of the babysitter at the centre of the Michael Kennedy statutory rape controversy Friday asked the prosecutor to halt his investigation.

"Based on the advice of medical experts, we believe our daughter's health and well-being will be seriously and potentially permanently impaired if she is required to testify in this matter and endure the unrelenting media coverage which would result," the Verrochi family said through their attorney Robert Popeo.
"Therefore, we have requested the district attorney to end this investigation, respect our daughter's wish for privacy and allow us to move on with our lives," the Verrochi lawyer said.

Norfolk County District Attorney Jeffrey Locke could not be reached immediately for comment. Since April, he has been investigating possible statutory rape charges against the son of slain Sen. Robert Kennedy who allegedly had an affair with the Verrochis' daughter that began when she was 14 and babysitting for his children.

Now 19 and a student at Boston University, the babysitter has refused to cooperate with Locke. Meanwhile, her parents, who were friends of the Kennedy family and neighbours in the wealthy south shore community of Cohassett, said in their statement:
"Michael Kennedy has caused us great pain and suffering by his outrageous conduct and his breach of trust we placed in him as a neighbour and friend."
Kennedy has also caused problems for his brother, Congressman Joseph Kennedy, who has seen his popularity plunge.

The Massachusetts Democrat, who has said he will seek his party's nomination for governor in next year's race, spent a large part of his speech to the state's Democratic convention June 7 apologising for his brother's behaviour and his own.

He told the delegates he was sorry both for his conduct toward his first wife, Sheila Rauch Kennedy - who has accused him of bullying her into an annulment - and for the scandal involving his brother.

A poll 400 registered voters released Thursday found 60 percent thought the apology was political. The survey, which has a five point margin of error, found that the state's Attorney General Scott Harshbarger would be the stronger Democratic candidate against either expected Republican nominee, Lt. Gov. Paul Cellucci or state Treasurer Joseph Malone.
